newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF MONACO PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF MONACO PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of Monaco players most likely to play in Saturday's French first division match against Marseille at the Louis II stadium.

Fabien Barthez, goalkeeper, age 25. Former Marseille keeper pushing PSG's Bernard Lama for France's number one shirt. Won his sixth cap against Sweden earlier this month. Superb reflexes and decisive coming out of goal.

Patrick Blondeau, right back, 29. From rough background in Marseille where could have turned to crime. Has broken into France squad this year late in his career. Good marker who likes to join attack at every opportunity.
Franck Dumas, central defender, 29. Team captain, strong, hard-tackling centre-back with keen positional sense, very difficult to get past.
Martin Djetou, central defender, 22. Young player who joined from Strasbourg in the close season to replace France international Lilian Thuram who left for Italy's Parma. One cap.
Lilian Martin, left back, 25. Done well as an understudy to long-term injury victim Eric Di Meco, has a good shot from free-kicks.

Emmanuel Petit, libero or defensive midfielder, 26. Has played more than 200 league games for his only club since rising up through the ranks. Fine positional sense and good distributor of the ball. A strong physical presence. Coming back from a knee injury. Has 15 French caps.

Philippe Leonard, utility defender or midfielder, 22. Belgian international who joined from Standard Liege in the off-season and has alternated between spells in the team and on the bench. Has recently returned from long injury layoff.
Sylvain Legwinski, defensive midfielder, 23. Product of club's junior sides, busy player who compensates for apparent physical fragility with good positional sense and never-say-die spirit.
Ali Benarbia, playmaker, 28. Has had fine season dictating play in the absence of Belgian Enzo Scifo. Has excellent vision. resumes as playmaker with Scifo called up for international duties.

Thierry Henry, striker, 19. Brilliant teenager nurtured by the club, now caught in the middle of a tug-of-war with Spain's Real Madrid. Given his league debut in 1994 when he had barely turned 17 by current Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger.

Sonny Anderson, striker, 26. Brazilian emblem of Monaco's title hopes who has already contributed a club top score of 17 league goals, averaging one every two matches. Opportunist with fine ball skills.
Gilles Grimandi, midfielder, 26. A useful midfielder, Grimandi missed the UEFA Cup seminfinal return leg against Internazionale through suspension.

Dan Petersen, striker, 24. The Danish striker, formerly with Ajax, promised plenty when he joined Monaco in 1994 but achieved little. Gifted but erratic, he will probably leave the club at the end of the season.
